  MINUTES
  ALHAMBRA CITY COUNCIL
  Special Meeting
  March 4, 2025
  9:00 a.m.

ROLL CALL: At 9:13 a.m., on Tuesday, March 4, 2025, the Alhambra City Council met in Ruth Reese
Hall of the Alhambra Civic Center Library, 101 South First Street, Alhambra, California.

CITY COUNCIL:  PRESENT:  MAZA, MALONEY, WANG, ANDRADE-STADLER, LEE
  ABSENT:  NONE

Officials Present: City Manager Binnquist, Assistant City Manager Garcia, Deputy City Manager
Stover, City Attorney Montes, City Clerk Myles, Director of Parks & Recreation Macias, Director of
Library Services LohGuan, Director of Public Works/Utilities Ray, Director of Finance Lieu, Director of
Human Resources Ko, Director of Community Development Ho, Fire Chief Ragusa, Chief of Police
Kennedy, Deputy Director of Public Works/Utilities Ahlen, Manager Analyst Alvarez

Also present was Facilitator William R. Kelly, President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group

CITY CLERK REPORT - NOTICE NO. N2M25-23
The City Clerk hereby reported that she duly gave notice of the Special Meeting of the City Council
being held this morning pursuant to the order of the Mayor and in accordance with Section 54956 of
the Government Code of the State of California.

1.  CITY COUNCIL STRATEGIC PLANNING SESSION – F2M25-28

  The City Council, City Manager, Department Heads and Facilitator William R. Kelly,
  President/CEO of Kelly Associates Management Group, held a strategic planning session. The
  strategic planning session included, but was not limited to, a discussion of the
  Councilmembers’ SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats) Analysis
  Survey results; and, setting tentative goal definitions and priorities.

  Public Comment:
  1) Victor DORADO, 901 Novelda Rd., expressed concerns regarding recent legislation at the
  State level which would usurp the City’s authority. He urged Council to consider supporting
  other cities opposing bill SB677. He continued to discuss the need for greater transparency for
  new development projects on the City’s website and urged resistance to development projects
  that would go against the community’s desires or the preservation of historic buildings.

  2) Lewis McCAMMON, 105 N. Cordova St., discussed the Community Opinion survey from True
  North facilitating the development of affordable housing. He went on to discuss the services
  offered by the Housing Rights Center and suggested that the City work with another agency to
  provide information to tenants and landlords in a timelier manner.

  3) Alison MORENA, Joanna VARGAS & Jonthan GUTIERREZ, representing the Alhambra
  Downtown Business Association, shared the progress of the business district over the last four
  years and the many programs developed by the Chamber of Commerce. They also provided

  1
3-4-25
   updates as to new businesses coming to Alhambra and made suggestions for improvements
  such as updated lighting infrastructure, clearer way finder signs, expanded Tree Lighting
  Ceremony event, greater environmental sustainability measures, and for the City to work
  closely with the business community.

  4) Shirley TATSUNO, 1408 S. Fifth St., expressed concern regarding recent business closures
  and suggested new businesses to attract to Alhambra such as Trader Joe’s and Daiso. She
  also discussed the lack of foot traffic on the east side of Main Street, the recent craft fair event,
  and the incoming Dollar Tree store and the public art pieces.

  5) John BWARIE, CEO of the Alhambra Chamber of Commerce, suggested the City focus on
  Economic Development, encouraged bold actions, and stated that this was an opportunity to
  move the City forward in a new direction. He suggested that the City work towards becoming
  one of the most business friendly cities in the San Gabriel Valley. He further suggested micro
  grant programs for business improvements, business relief fund, shop local programs,
  business recognition programs, an Economic Development Committee within the City Council,
  and a business accelerator program.

  Discussion: Mr. KELLY began the review of the most current 2024 Strategic Plan
  document, last updated and received by the City Council on January 27, 2025 and stated that
  there were no suggestions to change goals 1 – 6, and proceeded to discuss each Goal with
  Council. Mr. KELLY first led discussion regarding Goal 1 – Enhance Public Safety.
  Councilmember WANG discussed Goal 1.2 and made suggestions to expand the
  Neighborhood Watch program and emergency preparedness programs. Councilmember
  ANDRADE-STADLER also spoke regarding the importance of a Neighborhood Watch
  program and supported Ms. Wang’s comments. Vice Mayor MALONEY expressed his belief
  that the community wanted to go beyond the Neighborhood Watch program to address general
  public safety issues within the community such as emergency preparedness. He stated that
  there needed to be more discussion as to how to implement such a program and the City’s
  level of involvement. Mayor LEE suggested that the Neighborhood Watch program continue
  to oversee public safety and that there be a separate video educational program for the public
  regarding emergency preparedness. She suggested a continuation of CERT training
  programs. Ms. LEE went on to discuss emergency preparedness.

  Councilmember MAZA discussed Objective 1.1 regarding recruitment and maintaining a
  competitive Police Department. Mr. MALONEY and City Manager BINNQUIST discussed the
  ongoing goal in terms of recruiting and maintaining quality public safety in general. Ms.
  BINNQUIST further discussed the challenges involved in recruitment and maintaining both
  Police and Fire staff. Mr. KELLY suggested removing this Objective due to its constant ongoing
  nature as an integral part of continued operation as well as the constant challenges faced by
  all cities. Objective 1.1 was removed from the Strategic Plan Goal #1.

  Council continued with the Objectives under Goal 2 – Improve Infrastructure and Mobility. Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER discussed Objective 2.1 and suggested free service for students as well
  as expanding routes to reach the parks and the Community Center. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  went on to review several Objectives under Goal 2 including 2.3, 2.4, 2.5, 2.6, 2.7, 2.8, and
  2.12. For Objective 2.6, she suggested moving funds to other projects since the funding for
  the Bike/Ped Plan was pending. For Objective 2.8, she suggested pursing land use for more
  greenspace rather than new housing development. For Objective 2.11, she suggested
  increased priority for this project and continued to speak to the importance of traffic calming
  policies. Mr. KELLY and Ms. BINNQUIST provided a status update for Objective 2.11.

  Regarding Objective 2.1, Ms. WANG made suggestions for expanding the ACT Bus service to
  the south side of the City and made suggestions for providing more specific metrics for

  2
3-4-25
   measuring success in accomplishing the Strategic Plan Goals. Ms. WANG went on to discuss
  her concerns regarding delays to Objective 2.4 and rising construction costs, expanding
  Objective 2.7 to include earthquake retrofitting of critical City facilities, and agreed with Ms.
  Andrade-Stadler’s support on Objective 2.11.

  Mr. MALONEY suggesting reviewing items which had significant progress made and removing
  those from the Strategic Plan. Mr. MALONEY, Mr. KELLY, and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed
  progress on Objectives 2.2 and 2.3. Mr. MALONEY went on to discuss progress on Objective
  2.4, Objective 2.5, and Objective 2.6 with Ms. BINNQUIST. Mr. MALONEY supported Ms.
  Wang’s suggestions regarding Objective 2.7, suggested pursuing more pocket parks under
  Objective 2.8, and suggested seeking assistance from agencies such as the Wildlife
  Conservation Board for Objective 2.9. Mr. MALONEY went on to discuss Objective 2.10 and
  suggested creating more cohesive branding of City signage. Mr. KELLY received consensus
  from Council to incorporate Mr. Maloney’s suggestions for Objective 2.10.

  Mr. MAZA suggested adding an Objective to clean and maintain City parking structures and
  sidewalks in Downtown Alhambra and Ms. BINNQUIST further discussed the City’s current
  practices. Mr. MALONEY and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the assessment of Downtown
  Alhambra and other business district assessments. Ms. WANG supported the additional
  Objective and suggested expanding it to Valley Boulevard. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  supported the suggestion.

  Ms. LEE and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed Objective 2.1 to include the Senior Ride service in
  the consultant’s review. Ms. LEE also discussed the progress on other Objectives, urged
  greater construction of Bus shelters, discussed Objective 2.7 with Ms. BINNQUIST, supported
  more pocket parks under Objective 2.8 as well as encouraging business developments to
  include more greenspace, and suggested review of other areas for High Visibility Crosswalks
  in the City.

RECESS & RECONVENE:  Mayor LEE called for a brief recess at 10:45 a.m. and the meeting
resumed with all Councilmembers present at 10:55 a.m.

  Mr. KELLY requested Council comment on any additions under Goal 3 – Create Strong
  Financial Base and Strong Economic Base. Ms. LEE, Ms. BINNQUIST and Mr. KELLY
  discussed Objective 3.1. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER suggested changing Objective 3.4 to 30%
  and discussed Objective 3.5 and utilizing industrial areas for manufacturing. Ms. WANG
  discussed Objective 3.3 and suggested creating infographics to help residents understand the
  process. She also discussed Objective 3.5 and suggested better ways to define the outcome
  and track progress. She echoed Mr. Maloney’s suggestions to remove items from the Strategic
  Plan, and further suggested that those items be reclassified as “Achievement Goals.” Ms.
  ANDRADE-STADLER made further suggestions under Objective 3.7 regarding incentives to
  businesses which have left the City to return to vacant properties. Mr. MALONEY discussed
  progress on Objective 3.5 with Ms. BINNQUIST, discussed vacant properties on Chapel to
  Almansor as well as other areas on Valley Blvd., expanding the business assessment area,
  using the plans for East Main Street as a model for Valley Blvd., and discussed Objective 3.10
  with Ms. BINNQUIST and Mr. KELLY. Council further discussed Objective 3.10 as it related to
  3.4 with Ms. BINNQUIST. Ms. LEE supported using City reserves to pay down pension liability.
  Council agreed to leave the Objectives on the Strategic Plan.

  Ms. LEE suggested an additional Objective for a Shop Local Program. Council agreed with
  the addition. Mr. MAZA supported Ms. Wang and Ms. Andrade-Stadler’s suggestions and
  discussed them. Mr. MAZA suggested the removal of Objective 3.7 and 3.9. Mr. MALONEY
  suggested consolidating the Objectives. Ms. BINNQUIST stated that staff would address

  3
3-4-25
   comments and provide more information.

  Council discussed Objectives under Goal 4 – Enhance Transparency and Open Governance.
  Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER supported Objective 4.2. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER, Ms.
  BINNQUIST, and City Attorney MONTES discussed consistent rules of decorum and operation
  for all Board and Commissions.

  Regarding transparency and assisting the public who were not a part of social media, Ms.
  LEE discussed the use of digital billboards at major intersections to provide information to
  residents. Ms. WANG and Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER also discussed Ms. Lee’s suggestion.
  Mr. MALONEY did not fully support Ms. Lee’s suggestion, but provided additional suggestions
  for digital monitors at public locations. Ms. WANG supported the idea of more outreach and
  suggested more physical bulletin boards at public locations to post city flyers at a lower cost
  than digital boards. Mr. KELLY and Ms. LEE discussed where to add the suggestion under the
  Strategic Plan. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Mr. MAZA discussed the possibility of adding
  more information or a community calendar to the Around Alhambra. Mr. MAZA discussed staff
  assisting and educating senior citizen residents to use digital boards or interactive boards. Mr.
  MAZA continued to discuss the digital board at Joslyn Center.

  Mr. MALONEY suggested revisiting the idea of creating an Alhambra app to help residents
  access information, submit forms, and see a Community Calendar. Ms. WANG supported Mr.
  Maloney’s suggestion and further suggested staff review apps created by other cities for
  resident use as well as internal use to provide updates to residents. Mr. MALONEY further
  made suggestions for better informational materials such as providing materials in multiple
  languages.

  Mr. KELLY moved on to Goal 5, and Mr. MALONEY suggested combining 5.1 and 5.3. Ms.
  BINNQUIST provided an update to the progress on the EV Charging Stations. Ms. WANG
  suggested creating more EV Charging stations in business corridors to encourage economic
  development.

  Mr. KELLY went on to Goal 6. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER and Ms. BINNQUIST discussed the
  removal of Objectives 6.4, 6.5, and 6.7. Ms. BINNQUIST stated regarding Objective 6.8 that
  staff intended to present information regarding a TOT tax. Ms. ANDRADE-STADLER
  discussed Objective 6.2 with Ms. BINNQUIST regarding services provided by the Housing
  Rights Center. Mr. MAZA also discussed the importance of Objective 6.2. Mr. MAZA went on
  to discuss Objective 6.1

  Mr. KELLY and Ms. BINNQUIST stated that staff would return with a summation of comments
  made at this session and a draft 2025 Strategic Plan for Council’s review at a special meeting
  on Thursday, March 13, 2025.

ADJOURNMENT:  At 11:56 a.m., Mayor LEE adjourned the meeting.

  LAUREN MYLES, CMC
  CITY CLERK
  by
  BRIANNA LAMB MCCARTHY
  ASSISTANT CITY CLERK
